subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Protons in the nucleus
hotspots.description: The red particles packed in the dense core are the protons. They sit at the atom's center, bundled together with neutrons.
hotspots.positionHint: The cluster of red spheres at the center of the cutaway atom.
hotspots.function: Shows the protons packed in the atom's nucleus.

hotspots.label: Positive charge
hotspots.description: Each proton carries a +1 positive charge. Together the protons give the whole nucleus its positive charge.
hotspots.positionHint: The glow field around the nucleus, visible when the pulls-electrons layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the positive charge carried by each proton.

hotspots.label: The count that names the element
hotspots.description: Count the highlighted protons — this number is the element's identity. The periodic table's atomic number is this exact count.
hotspots.positionHint: The protons, individually highlighted when the proton-count layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows that proton count defines the element.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A cutaway atom floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: soft red protons and muted gray neutrons bundled together; electron cloud: a large faint translucent warm-white shell. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the proton highlight (coral / amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Protons: soft muted red spheres, roughness ~0.4. Neutrons: soft muted gray spheres, roughness ~0.4. Electron cloud: large translucent warm-white shell, alpha ~0.15. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: an atom cutaway focused on the proton, built to be read as 'the positive particle in the nucleus that names the element.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a cutaway atom — a dense nucleus cluster at center (a bundle of ~6 soft muted red proton spheres radius ~0.22 and ~6 soft muted gray neutron spheres radius ~0.22, packed together, one quadrant cut away for visibility) and a large faint translucent warm-white sphere (radius ~1.6, alpha ~0.15) representing the electron cloud, with a gap between nucleus and cloud.

2) PROTON COUNT (toggleable layer): the protons pulse briefly one at a time in sequence (app-driven highlight), drawing attention to each red particle as the count runs 1,2,3...

3) PULLS ELECTRONS (toggleable layer): a soft outward-from-nucleus gradient glow appears (app-rendered) with faint arrows from the nucleus toward the cloud, suggesting the positive charge attracting the electrons.

Camera: framed so the nucleus is clearly visible within the cloud; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: NucleusCluster, Protons_06, Neutrons_06, ElectronCloud, CutawayPlane, ChargeGlow. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
